name: dead hand
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The dead hand is an object of Irish folklore. An old belief held that a hand cut from a dead person carried great magical power. The most potent hands came from a victim of murder, an executed criminal, or a child. Thieves believed a dead hand protected them from capture. A thief carrying a dead hand could not be caught. The same hand worked wonders in the dairy. If one stirred cream nine times with the hand, a huge amount of butter would form.
objective: The dead hand of Irish folklore and the magic it held for thieves and for the making of butter.
key_results: A dead hand was believed to carry great magical power.
The best hands came from murder victims, executed criminals, or children.
A thief carrying a dead hand could not be caught.
Stirring cream nine times with the hand made butter form.
